title: REQ-4 (an empty cart cannot be checked out) is not implemented anywhere
evidence: src/cart.py holds only total() and discounted(). There is no checkout function and no emptiness check. docs/requirements.md:9 states the rule. grep of the three files finds no 'checkout' in code.
failing_case: A caller with an empty cart calls total([]) and gets 0, then proceeds to pay 0. Nothing refuses it, so the written rule is contradicted.
remediation: Add a checkout entry point that raises or returns an explicit error when the cart is empty, and have every caller go through it.

title: Money is summed as binary floats with no rounding or display rule, so REQ-3 has no implementation
evidence: total([0.1, 0.2]) evaluates to 0.30000000000000004 in Python floats. Nothing in src/ rounds or formats to two decimals (docs/requirements.md:5).
failing_case: A UI that shows str(total([0.1, 0.2])) displays 0.30000000000000004. Sums of many prices drift by fractions of a cent, and the total can differ from the sum of the displayed line prices.
remediation: Hold prices as integer cents or Decimal, quantise to 0.01 in one named function, and have the view call only that function.

title: discounted() accepts any percent, so a negative percent raises the price instead of reducing it
evidence: REQ-2 (docs/requirements.md:4) says a code reduces the total. For percent=-50, (100 - -50)/100 = 1.5, so discounted(10, -50) returns 15.0. The function never validates 0 <= percent <= 100. percent > 100 is silently floored, which hides a bad code.
failing_case: A discount code with a negative or mistyped percentage, such as -50, charges 15 on a 10 cart with no error.
remediation: Reject percent outside 0..100 at the boundary where codes are loaded, and have discounted() raise ValueError. Add tests for -1 and 101.

requirement.why: REQ-2 says a code reduces the total; it does not say what a negative percent should do, so the range is inferred from 'reduces'.

title: The only discount test covers the floor, so the percentage reduction in REQ-2 is unprotected
evidence: Every case in test_discount_floor has a result of 0 because of max(0, ...). Traced mutants that still pass: '[redacted]'; 'max(0, total_ - percent)' (10 - 150 gives 0); 'max(0, total_ * (100 - percent))' with the /100 dropped (10 * -50 gives 0). No test uses a percent in 1..99.
failing_case: discounted(100, 10) could return 90, 99, 0 or 100 and the suite stays green. A wrong discount charges customers the wrong amount.
remediation: Add cases such as discounted(100, 10) == 90, discounted(10, 0) == 10 and discounted(10, 100) == 0, so the formula and both edges are pinned.

title: test_rounding applies the two-decimal formatting itself, so it cannot fail on a rounding bug in the code
evidence: The :.2f is in the test, not in src/cart.py. Any total within 0.005 of 0.30 gives '0.30'. Traced mutant: changing total to return sum(prices) + 0.001 gives 0.301, which formats as '0.30' and the test still passes. Sandbox bash was denied, so this is traced, not executed.
failing_case: total() returns 0.30000000000000004 or 0.301 and test_rounding still passes. REQ-3 (two decimals shown) is never exercised in product code.
remediation: Move formatting into a named function in src/ (for example format_price) and assert on its output; test it with values that round up, round down and sit on a half-cent.

title: test_empty_checkout is labelled REQ-4 but asserts the opposite behaviour
evidence: The test (tests/test_cart.py:16-17) checks that an empty cart totals 0. REQ-4 (docs/requirements.md:9) says an empty cart cannot be checked out. The test passes on the current code and would also pass if checkout were wholly missing, as it is.
failing_case: Any implementation that lets an empty cart through to payment still passes this test, so the suite reports REQ-4 as covered while it is not.
remediation: Assert the refusal: pytest.raises on the checkout call with an empty cart. Keep a separate test for total([]) == 0 under REQ-1 if wanted.
